cues: Care against control: the story never says Rakesh is medically wrong, but asks what a life is worth if it is lived only to eat medicines.
Appearance and reality: the same behaviour is admired in the first half and called tyranny in the second; as the narrator admits, only the interpretation has altered.
Ambition and its cost: in the new prosperity there is no room for the old man's tastes, or even his name.
And old age: Varma does not want more life; he wants his exhaustion respected.
